land.text: Opobo, where Jubo Jubogha (Jaja) moved 'due to a civil war in Bonny'

predecessors.note: The Bonny page: 'In 1869 a major battle between the two factions led to Ja-Ja founding a new state at Opobo'.

land.text: Opobo, under the Council of Chiefs chaired by Perekule from September 1887

successors.note: The Opobo page does not explain why Jaja's rule ended in September 1887; no date for the end of the city-state.

correction.text: Opobo, the city-state on the Imo estuary founded by Jaja in 1870

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area and no extent; a 20 km circle round Opobo stands for it.

ledger.note: 1870 (25 December): Jaja is installed at Opobo. 'In 1870, Jubo first arrived in what is now Opobo, having moved there due to a civil war in Bonny'; the rulers table gives '25 December 1870' as the start of Jubo Jubogha's rule as Jaja I.

1887 (September): Jaja's rule ends. The rulers table lists 'September 1887 | 1891 | Perekule (chairman Council of Chiefs)'; the page does not say why, nor that the British took Opobo, nor when the city-state ended. The transfer to the Oil Rivers (Niger Coast) Protectorate is the researcher's reading (confidence 1).
1887 (September): the independent city-state of Jaja ends; the community continues with kings (Obiesigha Jaja II 1893-1915, Dipiri 1916-1936, Sodienye Jaja III, Dandeson Douglas Jaja V 2004-2025).

sources.title: Opobo
sources.note: Jaja at Opobo from 1870, rule from 25 December 1870; September 1887 change of ruler; later kings; no 1884 treaty, no exile, no extent.

sources.title: Bonny Kingdom
sources.note: The 1869 battle and the founding of Opobo.

notes: The Kingdom of Opobo has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened; the Opobo page gives no extent, no treaty, no exile of Jaja and no end date for the city-state, so the end is the date of the change of ruler (September 1887) read as the end of independence at confidence 1. The Wikipedia article is 'Opobo' (a community and former city-state in Rivers State). Not on the pages: Jaja's treaty of 1873, the 1884 protectorate, his arrest and exile (1887), the Imo River trade.
